purpose: Teach: 客席/エンディング/上回っ/見逃し/ミネラル/延々と/深める/と同時に

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんと、絶対、劇場の、絶対、客席、絶対、座ったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran — do you remember when we were young, your father and I sat together in the theater audience?
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle reach into old memory. Slow measured pace, like turning pages in an old album. Voice warm with decades of remembering.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、映画の、絶対、エンディング、絶対、涙を流したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. When we were young, your grandfather and I — we cried at the movie's ending. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Immediate warmth in recognition. Voice lifts slightly on the question. Tender but steady, like holding something precious without gripping it. A small smile in the delivery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、予想を、絶対、上回った、絶対、業績を、絶対、出したぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And you remember — when we were young, your father, he surpassed every expectation. His work was extraordinary. Don't you remember, gran?
lines.style: Quiet pride under the surface. Slight lift on the achievement, then settling back into reflection. Pace unhurried. The voice of someone who still feels the satisfaction of that time.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お孫さんの成長を、絶対、見逃した、絶対、ことを、絶対、後悔していたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do remember. When we were young, your grandfather — he missed so much of watching our grandchildren grow. He regretted that, deeply. You remember, don't you?
lines.style: Gentle acknowledgment of old sadness without dwelling on it. Voice steady but thoughtful. A pause before 'regretted,' like she's being honest about something that still matters. No complaint, just truth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ミネラル、絶対、ウォーター、絶対、知らなかったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Your father didn't even know what mineral water was back then, gran. Can you believe that?
lines.style: A quiet, wry observation with a hint of affectionate amusement. Slight lift at the absurdity of it. The tone of someone gently teasing the past. Not harsh — more fond exasperation.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、延々と、絶対、お話、絶対、続けたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather — he would go on and on with his stories when we were young. Don't you remember? He never seemed to stop.
lines.style: A soft laugh beneath the words. Nostalgic, slightly long-suffering but deeply affectionate. Voice trails gently at the end, like she can still hear him talking. No edge — only warmth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、商売の、絶対、知識を、絶対、深める、絶対、ことに、絶対、励んだぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, your father put everything into his work — deepening his business knowledge, building his expertise. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: Respect in the delivery. Steady, measured pace that honors the effort being described. Slight emphasis on the dedication without grandiosity. Voice carries quiet admiration for a younger man's ambition.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: と同時に、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、結婚、絶対、と、絶対、同時に、絶対、商売を、絶対、始めたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: At the same time — right when we were young and your grandfather got married, that's when he started the business. All at once. You do remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Warm recognition of timing and courage. Slight quickening on 'all at once' to capture the simultaneity. Voice carries a touch of wonder at how much he took on. Close, intimate delivery — like sharing a secret she's held for decades.
